question: What does prefabrication depend on, and what is the evidence?

answer.answer:
Prefabrication (PR2) has two requirements it cannot proceed without, precise up-front planning and logistics (RI14) and a regulatory route for offsite compliance resting on third-party certification and traceability (RI18), and three upstream enablers that bring it about: DfMA for DFAB process (PR9), early contractor involvement (CO11) and an integrated supply chain (VA14). Not one of the five is a machine: they are planning, regulatory, design-method and organisational conditions, so what prefabrication asks for is process and contract work, not equipment. The five are not equal in the record either: 36 of the 50 coded cases draw on precise planning against 12 on the regulatory concern, and all five paths are backed by peer-reviewed evidence, with what prefabrication returns being schedule (VA2), quality (VA3), site safety (VA13) and fewer errors (VA10). No deployed project record sits in the material behind this answer, so the finding rests on the coded case counts and the literature, and the record frames these as graded dependency edges rather than in the words dependence or evidence.

**What PR2 depends on**

PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site" (Process) carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all of them listed in the context, and 20 of the 50 coded cases draw on PR2 itself. [1] That makes the following set exact rather than a sample.

Two edges run outward from PR2 to a requirement, which in a dependsOn relation places the far end upstream in practice:

- DEP33: PR2 dependsOn RI14 "Rely on precise planning", on the ground that prefabrication relies on precise up-front planning and logistics, graded peer-reviewed [2], and carried by 18 of the 50 coded cases [1]. RI14 is itself drawn on by 36 of the 50 coded cases [1], making it the heaviest thing in this set.
- DEP96: PR2 dependsOn RI18 "Regulatory/legal concern", where a functional regulatory system for offsite compliance requires third-party certification and traceability, graded peer-reviewed [3], carried by 10 of the 50 [1]. RI18 is drawn on by 12 of the 50 coded cases and carries 5 inbound edges, all listed [1]: the other four, from CO6, AT3, PR3 and PR8, are the standard-graded ones, and of the 8 standard-graded edges in the whole graph, which are listed complete [1], none touches PR2. Prefabrication's regulatory tie is asserted from the peer-reviewed literature, not from a cited code.

Three edges run into PR2 from enablers upstream of it:

- DEP15: PR9 "DfMA for DFAB process" enablesCapability PR2, DfMA orienting the project toward offsite manufacture, peer-reviewed [4], carried by 15 of the 50 [1]; PR9 is drawn on by 15 of the 50 coded cases [1].
- DEP22: CO11 "Early contractor involvement" enablesCapability PR2, since integrating manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design requires the delivering production party to be involved in the early design phase, peer-reviewed [5], carried by 13 of the 50 [1]; CO11 is drawn on by 14 of the 50 [1].
- DEP79: VA14 "Integrate supply chain" enablesCapability PR2, supply chain integration supporting the offsite production line, peer-reviewed, carried by 12 of the 50 [1]; VA14 is drawn on by 14 of the 50 [1].

The fourth inbound edge runs the other way logically: DEP55 has PR4 "Robotic assembly" hasPrecondition PR2, automated overhead delivery and assembly requiring extensive prefabrication and unification of materials, peer-reviewed, carried by 4 of the 50 [1]. There PR2 is the requirement, not the dependent, so robotic assembly sits downstream of prefabrication. PR4 is drawn on by 13 of the 50 [1], and the edge is carried by only 4, so the two are far less often paired than either is used.

**What it returns**

DEP17: PR2 enablesCapability VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency", offsite work compressing schedule [6], carried by 19 of the 50 [1]; DEP18 to VA3 "Improve quality/performance" through the controlled factory environment [7], carried by 18 [1]; DEP80 to VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints", factory production improving quality control and reducing rework [8], carried by 14 [1]; DEP19 to VA13 "Improve site safety", moving work offsite improving site safety [9], carried by 12 [1]. All four are peer-reviewed. Of PR2's own outbound value edges, the safety path is the least often carried, even though 39 of the 50 coded cases draw on VA13 in their own right [1], so most safety gains in the record arrive by routes other than this one.

**Limits**

The 1-hop expansion also lists many coOccursWith links from PR2, to artefacts, other processes and risks. Those are statistical association only, not asserted dependency, and should not be read as requirements. The cited dependency layer is sparse and uneven, 100 edges touching 68 of the 140 enablers, which is a property of the literature rather than of the record [1], so enablers with no edge can still matter: RE6 "Significant human involvement" is drawn on by 50 of the 50 coded cases and carries no dependency edge at all [1]. The retrieved material carries no deployed Process RP record, census record or firm for prefabrication, so nothing here rests on a named deployment.
